events.detail: no proposer takes it yet: its end is not anchored
no-return-no-prologue: no return and no push {.., lr}

rules.recovers: nearby calls misread as far jumps, which would glue a neighbouring function into the caller
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits bl as a jump only when the target is beyond the range of `b`; the shortest far jump in five ROMs is 1,960 bytes
rules.summary: a bl closer than farJump.minDistance to its target (the far-jump idiom fails) is a call

rules.recovers: functions proposed inside another function's unreached branch arms or alignment padding
rules.restsOn: a compiled function is one contiguous run, so the few bytes inside it the walk never reached are still its own; a table of entry stubs `movs rX, #k; b T` that share one tail gives each entry its own constant, so an unreached copy of the entry stub is another entry, not dead code
rules.summary: a dense function's free bytes inside its extent are claimed as dead code, except unreached copies of its own `movs rX, #k; b T` entry stub

rules.recovers: functions reached only through computed addresses or not at all (dead code, callbacks named in data the harvest missed)
rules.restsOn: compiled functions are laid out back to back, so an unreferenced one starts where the previous one ends, give or take alignment; a literal pool word holding an accepted Thumb function + 1 is that function's address, not code
rules.summary: a valid Thumb reading at the cursor, first word nonzero and no pointer to an accepted function, extent inside [gap start, end), chained forward from the gap start

rules.recovers: functions after padding or a callback table inside a gap, without walking through data that would chain false entries
rules.restsOn: between compiled functions sit only alignment zeros and small tables of Thumb code pointers; other bytes are data
rules.summary: the forward chain steps 4 bytes over a zero word or an odd word pointing into the ROM, and stops at anything else

rules.recovers: SoundMainRAM and other mixers on all five tuning ROMs
rules.restsOn: hand-written mixers keep ARM blocks and tables inside a Thumb function, so their extent has holes and their paths may not balance the stack
rules.summary: a gap's head reads as a function failing at most density or stack balance, with at least gapScan.minInsns instructions, its code inside the gap

rules.recovers: the call graph below every accepted function
rules.restsOn: a bl (or a bx after mov lr, pc) that settles as a call enters a function
rules.summary: the targets of the calls of an accepted function are functions

rules.recovers: data and text decoded as code
rules.restsOn: every path of a compiled function decodes until it returns or jumps away
rules.summary: the walk from the entry decodes at least one instruction and hits no decode error

rules.recovers: runs of data that decode without ever returning
rules.restsOn: a compiled function either returns or pushes lr before calling what never returns
rules.summary: the reading returns somewhere, or opens with push {.., lr}
